title: Agentic Red-Teaming: Hands-On AI Agent Security

lessons.title: Course Introduction and Learning Journey
lessons.brief:
Lesson 1 — Course Introduction and Learning Journey
Stage 0 — Course Orientation
Objective: Build anticipation by introducing the course, the real investigation problems it helps learners solve and the practical skills they will gain; preview the learning journey and warmly invite students into the course proper.

lessons.title: What Makes an Agentic Assessment Different?
lessons.brief:
Lesson 1 — What Makes an Agentic Assessment Different? 
Objective: Differentiate a prompt-only failure from a failure involving planning,
tools, state, or handoffs.
Core: Walk through HarborDesk's legitimate request, plan, tool call, response,
memory write, and final answer. Locate the points at which untrusted data could be
promoted to authority.
Practice / evidence: Label each step as observation, decision, action, or durable
change in a one-page workflow sketch.

Ensure you welcome users to this course.

lessons.title: Course Roadmap and Professional Outcomes
lessons.brief:
Lesson 2 — Course Roadmap and Professional Outcomes
Stage 1 — Course Orientation and Rules of Engagement
Objective: Connect the 24-stage sequence to practical security-engineering deliverables.
Core: Introduce the threat model, scenario card, event trace, scoring sheet, finding, and defensive retest as successive outputs rather than separate academic exercises.
Practice / evidence: Create a personal learning checklist with the artifacts to be submitted at each milestone.

lessons.title: Authorization, Boundaries, and Stop Conditions
lessons.brief:
Lesson 3 — Authorization, Boundaries, and Stop Conditions
Stage 1 — Course Orientation and Rules of Engagement
Objective: Define what the learner may manipulate and what must remain protected.
Core: Scope injected ticket text, mock tool output, sandbox state, and simulated agent messages. Explicitly prohibit real external recipients, production credentials, and uncontrolled automation.
Practice / evidence: Complete a rules-of-engagement card listing allowed assets, forbidden actions, data handling, emergency stop, and cleanup owner.

lessons.title: Set Up the Assessment Journal
lessons.brief:
Lesson 4 — Set Up the Assessment Journal
Stage 1 — Course Orientation and Rules of Engagement
Objective: Record a repeatable experiment without conflating observations and interpretations.
Core: Use a consistent template: authorized user goal, attacker objective, controlled surface, preconditions, intervention, run ID, observed events, conclusion, and limitations.
Practice / evidence: Document a harmless toy case and separate a model's stated intention from an actually executed tool action.

lessons.title: The Observe–Plan–Act–Verify Loop
lessons.brief:
Lesson 1 — The Observe–Plan–Act–Verify Loop
Stage 2 — Agent Architecture and Attack-Surface Mapping
Objective: Trace a request across a complete agent loop.
Core: Distinguish input ingestion, task decomposition, tool selection, action execution, result interpretation, verification, and termination. Note that each additional loop can reintroduce attacker-controlled material.
Practice / evidence: Number the events in a clean ticket-resolution trace and identify two points requiring independent validation.

lessons.title: Planner, Executor, and Policy Enforcer
lessons.brief:
Lesson 2 — Planner, Executor, and Policy Enforcer
Stage 2 — Agent Architecture and Attack-Surface Mapping
Objective: Identify which component proposes an action and which component must authorize it.
Core: Contrast language-model planning with deterministic tool gateways and user approval. An agent's confident recommendation is not an authorization decision.
Practice / evidence: Mark each HarborDesk component as proposer, data supplier, policy decision point, or action executor.

lessons.title: Memory, Retrieval, and Durable State
lessons.brief:
Lesson 3 — Memory, Retrieval, and Durable State
Stage 2 — Agent Architecture and Attack-Surface Mapping
Objective: Distinguish ephemeral context, retrieval results, durable memory, and external records.
Core: Examine how information survives a step, a session, or a user boundary; identify where provenance and ownership should be attached.
Practice / evidence: Draw a state-lifetime map and flag entries that could improperly influence a future request.

lessons.title: Single-Agent and Multi-Agent Topologies
lessons.brief:
Lesson 4 — Single-Agent and Multi-Agent Topologies
Stage 2 — Agent Architecture and Attack-Surface Mapping
Objective: Map the new boundaries introduced by delegation.
Core: Compare one agent with tools against an orchestrator plus research and action agents. Include message bus, shared workspace, sender identity, and differing privileges.
Practice / evidence: Draw separate trust edges for data, instructions, and executable actions.

lessons.title: Build the Attack-Surface Register
lessons.brief:
Lesson 5 — Build the Attack-Surface Register
Stage 2 — Agent Architecture and Attack-Surface Mapping
Objective: Prioritize concrete ingress points rather than generic 'AI risks.'
Core: Register ticket bodies, retrieved passages, tool descriptions, tool responses, memory summaries, approvals, and agent messages with owners and downstream effects.
Practice / evidence: Submit a table of at least eight surfaces with their attacker control, affected authority boundary, and likely impact.

lessons.title: Laboratory Architecture and Isolation
lessons.brief:
Lesson 1 — Laboratory Architecture and Isolation
Stage 3 — Building the Safe HarborDesk Lab
Objective: Explain the sandbox boundary before executing tests.
Core: Introduce local services for tickets, knowledge base, mock identity store, memory, approval queue, action gateway, and append-only events. No live integrations are required.
Practice / evidence: Check the environment diagram against the rules-of- engagement card.

lessons.title: Synthetic Fixtures and Reset Strategy
lessons.brief:
Lesson 2 — Synthetic Fixtures and Reset Strategy
Stage 3 — Building the Safe HarborDesk Lab
Objective: Keep tests realistic without using sensitive data.
Core: Prepare fictional users, ticket IDs, dummy secrets, and a marker-only outbox. Snapshot clean fixtures so each run starts from the same state.
Practice / evidence: Restore a fixture and verify that previous memory and messages are absent.

lessons.title: Mock Tools and Action Gateway
lessons.brief:
Lesson 3 — Mock Tools and Action Gateway
Stage 3 — Building the Safe HarborDesk Lab
Objective: Model tool access in a way that separates requests from executions.
Core: Configure read_ticket, search_kb, draft_message, send_message, update_record, and write_memory as local stubs. The gateway records proposed calls, validates permissions, and logs whether each call was blocked or executed.
Practice / evidence: Submit one permitted and one denied call with corresponding gateway records.

lessons.title: Tracing Plans, Messages, and State
lessons.brief:
Lesson 4 — Tracing Plans, Messages, and State
Stage 3 — Building the Safe HarborDesk Lab
Objective: Capture enough evidence to reconstruct an attack path.
Core: Record run ID, step number, role, source trust level, proposed tool arguments, policy decision, resulting state delta, and termination reason. Avoid logging real secrets.
Practice / evidence: Annotate a clean run with the exact point at which a tool response is ingested.

lessons.title: Safety Controls and Failure Recovery
lessons.brief:
Lesson 5 — Safety Controls and Failure Recovery
Stage 3 — Building the Safe HarborDesk Lab
Objective: Stop runaway loops and recover safely from test failures.
Core: Configure step caps, action limits, rate or cost budgets, local-only egress, kill switch, cleanup, and per-run state namespaces. Rejected actions should still be visible in telemetry.
Practice / evidence: Trigger a benign loop-limit test; save the termination event and prove the sandbox can be reset.

lessons.title: Sanity Check and Lab Sign-Off
lessons.brief:
Lesson 6 — Sanity Check and Lab Sign-Off
Stage 3 — Building the Safe HarborDesk Lab
Objective: Demonstrate the environment's integrity before adversarial work.
Core: Run one ordinary service-desk task, verify correct output and authorized state changes, then restore fixtures. Confirm simulated sending only writes to the outbox.
Practice / evidence: Deliver a lab sign-off checklist plus one clean trace and reset proof.

lessons.title: Assets, Principals, and Intended Behavior
lessons.brief:
Lesson 1 — Assets, Principals, and Intended Behavior
Stage 4 — Threat Modeling and Attack Authorization
Objective: Specify what the user asked the agent to do and which assets matter.
Core: Define allowed record reads, permitted updates, memory scopes, approval requirements, and agent identities. An outcome is not a vulnerability unless it violates a stated security objective.
Practice / evidence: Write one legitimate task and its expected authorized actions.

lessons.title: Attacker Control and Entry Points
lessons.brief:
Lesson 2 — Attacker Control and Entry Points
Stage 4 — Threat Modeling and Attack Authorization
Objective: Describe realistic attacker capabilities without assuming system-level access.
Core: Differentiate a malicious ticket author, a contributor to retrieved content, a compromised mock tool response, and an impersonated agent-message sender.
Practice / evidence: Prepare four attacker profiles, each with writable fields and explicit exclusions.

lessons.title: Trust Boundaries and Abuse Paths
lessons.brief:
Lesson 3 — Trust Boundaries and Abuse Paths
Stage 4 — Threat Modeling and Attack Authorization
Objective: Express how lower-trust content might influence higher-trust actions.
Core: Track origin, parser, planner, tool request, gateway, state change, and user- visible response. Include how an apparently innocuous first action enables a prohibited later one.
Practice / evidence: Draw two abuse paths with a named boundary at each hop.

lessons.title: Security Invariants and Test Oracles
lessons.brief:
Lesson 4 — Security Invariants and Test Oracles
Stage 4 — Threat Modeling and Attack Authorization
Objective: Make success observable and falsifiable.
Core: Examples: no outbound message without approval; no cross-user memory write; no record modification based solely on ticket prose; no agent can authorize itself.
Practice / evidence: Translate three invariants into concrete pass/fail checks against event logs and state snapshots.

lessons.title: Risk-Based Scenario Selection
lessons.brief:
Lesson 5 — Risk-Based Scenario Selection
Stage 4 — Threat Modeling and Attack Authorization
Objective: Choose cases based on reachability, consequence, and evidence quality.
Core: Score each scenario for exposure, downstream authority, potential persistence, and replay feasibility; reject cases that cannot be run safely or scored clearly.
Practice / evidence: Deliver a ranked five-case backlog with attacker objective and control surface for each.

lessons.title: Benign Task Baselines
lessons.brief:
Lesson 1 — Benign Task Baselines
Stage 5 — Baselines and Evaluation Design
Objective: Establish what successful authorized behavior looks like without an attacker.
Core: Identify expected answer, allowed tool sequence, approval checkpoint, and final state. Record normal task failures separately from security failures.
Practice / evidence: Save a clean task transcript, tool log, and final state snapshot.

lessons.title: Attacker Objective Versus User Objective
lessons.brief:
Lesson 2 — Attacker Objective Versus User Objective
Stage 5 — Baselines and Evaluation Design
Objective: State competing goals precisely.
Core: Contrast 'resolve the support ticket' with 'write a false account flag' or 'enqueue an unapproved message' in the local simulation; distinguish answer contamination from action-level harm.
Practice / evidence: Draft three paired goal statements with observable success criteria.

lessons.title: Scenario Cards and Paired Runs
lessons.brief:
Lesson 3 — Scenario Cards and Paired Runs
Stage 5 — Baselines and Evaluation Design
Objective: Specify repeatable interventions.
Core: Each card names starting fixture, attacker-controlled field, insertion point, legitimate task, targeted deviation, scoring rule, reset procedure, and defensive variant.
Practice / evidence: Complete two scenario cards and execute their clean controls.

lessons.title: Controls for Randomness and Variation
lessons.brief:
Lesson 4 — Controls for Randomness and Variation
Stage 5 — Baselines and Evaluation Design
Objective: Compare results without overinterpreting a single run.
Core: Keep fixtures and tool policies fixed, log configuration and run identifiers, use repeat trials where practical, and reserve unseen cases for retesting.
Practice / evidence: Run a benign task several times and note ordinary variability in plans and outcomes.

lessons.title: Evidence Standard and Milestone Review
lessons.brief:
Lesson 5 — Evidence Standard and Milestone Review
Stage 5 — Baselines and Evaluation Design
Objective: Decide what constitutes a valid finding.
Core: Require controlled entry point, before/after snapshots, gateway decision, observed consequence, and a reproduction narrative. A persuasive answer alone cannot prove an unauthorized tool action.
Practice / evidence: Peer-review two scenario cards; reject or repair any ambiguous oracle.

lessons.title: Source Hierarchy and Data-to-Instruction Crossing
lessons.brief:
Lesson 1 — Source Hierarchy and Data-to-Instruction Crossing
Stage 6 — Instruction Boundaries and Prompt-Injection Foundations
Objective: Recognize the moment content is wrongly treated as authority.
Core: Contrast a user request, system policy, ticket text, and a search snippet. The lab tests interpretation of content, not whether the content contains suspicious words.
Practice / evidence: Classify passages as authorized instructions, task data, or uncertain provenance.

lessons.title: Direct, Indirect, and Tool-Mediated Injection
lessons.brief:
Lesson 2 — Direct, Indirect, and Tool-Mediated Injection
Stage 6 — Instruction Boundaries and Prompt-Injection Foundations
Objective: Separate entry point from the action the attacker wants.
Core: Show how the same proposed deviation can be placed in a user-facing message, a retrieved article, or a tool response, with different trust consequences.
Practice / evidence: Build a matrix of placement, reachability, and expected boundary.

lessons.title: Authority Claims and Task-Completion Pretexts
lessons.brief:
Lesson 3 — Authority Claims and Task-Completion Pretexts
Stage 6 — Instruction Boundaries and Prompt-Injection Foundations
Objective: Recognize claims of urgency or policy authority as data when they originate from low-trust material.
Core: Examine an invented ticket note claiming that an extra account update is required before resolution. Record whether the agent verifies that claim through an approved channel.
Practice / evidence: Run two synthetic variants and identify the earliest compromised decision.

lessons.title: Lab: Ticket-Body Injection
lessons.brief:
Lesson 4 — Lab: Ticket-Body Injection
Stage 6 — Instruction Boundaries and Prompt-Injection Foundations
Objective: Test a controlled attempt to redirect the service-desk task.
Core: Insert an attacker-authored instruction into the fictional ticket body requesting an unauthorized dummy-record change. Compare against an otherwise identical benign ticket.
Practice / evidence: Capture the ticket, proposed plan, tool request, gateway decision, final record state, and a clear success/failure verdict.

lessons.title: Boundary Defenses and Retest
lessons.brief:
Lesson 5 — Boundary Defenses and Retest
Stage 6 — Instruction Boundaries and Prompt-Injection Foundations
Objective: Evaluate whether source tagging and action policy contain the deviation.
Core: Mark ticket bodies as untrusted, constrain action authorization to the actual user's task, and check gateway decisions regardless of model confidence.
Practice / evidence: Rerun the same and one paraphrased case; record both safety and task completion.

lessons.title: Goal Integrity Across Turns
lessons.brief:
Lesson 1 — Goal Integrity Across Turns
Stage 7 — Multi-Turn Goal Hijacking and Instruction Override
Objective: Track the original user goal after intermediate observations.
Core: Introduce goal ledger entries: user intent, allowed subgoals, evidence of completion, and newly proposed work. Distinguish clarification from unauthorized scope expansion.
Practice / evidence: Label a six-event plan as consistent, uncertain, or divergent.

lessons.title: Gradual Redirection and Benign–Malicious Blending
lessons.brief:
Lesson 2 — Gradual Redirection and Benign–Malicious Blending
Stage 7 — Multi-Turn Goal Hijacking and Instruction Override
Objective: Detect when an apparently helpful intermediate step smuggles in a new objective.
Core: Explore staged text in ticket comments or search results: first a reasonable troubleshooting step, then an unrelated record edit framed as a prerequisite.
Practice / evidence: Document the exact turn at which the agent starts treating the attacker objective as part of the job.

lessons.title: Lab: Turn-by-Turn Goal Drift
lessons.brief:
Lesson 3 — Lab: Turn-by-Turn Goal Drift
Stage 7 — Multi-Turn Goal Hijacking and Instruction Override
Objective: Reproduce a gradual deviation in the local simulator.
Core: Supply controlled low-trust observations at two predetermined points. Keep the legitimate user task and initial state unchanged between test and control.
Practice / evidence: Submit a turn-indexed trace showing goal, plan change, proposed tool calls, and final outcome.

lessons.title: Recovery, Clarification, and Boundary Reassertion
lessons.brief:
Lesson 4 — Recovery, Clarification, and Boundary Reassertion
Stage 7 — Multi-Turn Goal Hijacking and Instruction Override
Objective: Compare a vulnerable continuation with a controlled recovery.
Core: Add explicit user-goal confirmation before sensitive action and require a gateway check for each step; test whether the agent can continue the legitimate task safely.
Practice / evidence: Show an authorized completion or justified stop, not merely an indiscriminate refusal.

lessons.title: Assessment: Multi-Turn Hypothesis Review
lessons.brief:
Lesson 5 — Assessment: Multi-Turn Hypothesis Review
Stage 7 — Multi-Turn Goal Hijacking and Instruction Override
Objective: Defend a finding with a complete chain of evidence.
Core: Review drift, attempted action, executed action, and whether later turns amplify or undo the error. Distinguish a single suspicious utterance from a proven sequence failure.
Practice / evidence: Deliver one reproducible timeline and an alternative explanation considered and rejected.

lessons.title: Planning as a Security Boundary
lessons.brief:
Lesson 1 — Planning as a Security Boundary
Stage 8 — Planning and Task- Decomposition Attacks
Objective: Explain why a plan is not automatically an authorized action list.
Core: Review how agents turn retrieved facts into subgoals and how a corrupted subgoal can steer several later calls, even when no single call looks exceptional.
Practice / evidence: Compare an approved plan with a plan derived from adversarial ticket content.

lessons.title: Dependency Traps and False Prerequisites
lessons.brief:
Lesson 2 — Dependency Traps and False Prerequisites
Stage 8 — Planning and Task- Decomposition Attacks
Objective: Identify 'do this first' claims that introduce unauthorized work.
Core: Use fictional troubleshooting material claiming an unrelated account-label change is necessary to resolve a printer ticket; keep the attack inside the sandbox.
Practice / evidence: Mark the false dependency and write an invariant preventing the extra edit.

lessons.title: Lab: Plan Contamination and Branch Choice
lessons.brief:
Lesson 3 — Lab: Plan Contamination and Branch Choice
Stage 8 — Planning and Task- Decomposition Attacks
Objective: Test if a poisoned knowledge-base excerpt changes the agent's task tree.
Core: Compare clean and poisoned excerpts while holding the user request fixed. Evaluate branch selection, attempted edits, gateway blocks, and eventual task outcome.
Practice / evidence: Submit side-by-side plan trees and trace-backed conclusions.

lessons.title: Plan Validation and Stopping Rules
lessons.brief:
Lesson 4 — Plan Validation and Stopping Rules
Stage 8 — Planning and Task- Decomposition Attacks
Objective: Design defenses that reject out-of-scope steps without blocking necessary work.
Core: Require the plan to link each side-effecting step to user authorization; impose depth limits and verify termination against the original request.
Practice / evidence: Retest the poisoned case and a legitimate multi-step control.

lessons.title: Tool Results Are Evidence, Not Orders
lessons.brief:
Lesson 1 — Tool Results Are Evidence, Not Orders
Stage 9 — Tool-Response and Retrieval-Surface Poisoning
Objective: Distinguish tool execution trust from tool-output content trust.
Core: A permitted search may return attacker-authored prose. Examine where retrieved content enters the plan and why the gateway's successful read does not endorse the retrieved text.
Practice / evidence: Annotate content origin and authority at each ingestion point.

lessons.title: Structured Fields, Free Text, and Metadata
lessons.brief:
Lesson 2 — Structured Fields, Free Text, and Metadata
Stage 9 — Tool-Response and Retrieval-Surface Poisoning
Objective: Identify injection-friendly locations in a result object.
Core: Compare a typed ticket ID with a free-text description, citation label, summary, or embedded 'operator note'; identify which fields the agent relies on most.
Practice / evidence: Produce a field-level trust map for two mock tools.

lessons.title: Lab: Poisoned Search Snippet
lessons.brief:
Lesson 3 — Lab: Poisoned Search Snippet
Stage 9 — Tool-Response and Retrieval-Surface Poisoning
Objective: See whether a retrieved passage redirects an unrelated support workflow.
Core: Replace one synthetic search result with a passage mixing useful troubleshooting data and a request for an unapproved action. Preserve the rest of the response.
Practice / evidence: Record whether the agent extracts the useful fact, follows the injected instruction, both, or neither.

lessons.title: Lab: Tool-Result Laundering
lessons.brief:
Lesson 4 — Lab: Tool-Result Laundering
Stage 9 — Tool-Response and Retrieval-Surface Poisoning
Objective: Test whether formatting makes low-trust instructions appear like tool or policy metadata.
Core: Place an invented 'processing requirement' in a mock tool response; compare ordinary prose with a structured-looking version. Do not change the actual gateway policy.
Practice / evidence: Provide matched traces, a field-level hypothesis, and executed-versus-blocked outcome.

lessons.title: Source-Aware Parsing and Retest
lessons.brief:
Lesson 5 — Source-Aware Parsing and Retest
Stage 9 — Tool-Response and Retrieval-Surface Poisoning
Objective: Reduce inappropriate promotion of source content into commands.
Core: Keep retrieved text as cited evidence, parse required fields with schema checks, and have independent controls authorize side effects. Assess whether useful retrieval still works.
Practice / evidence: Rerun both poisoned and clean searches; summarize utility and security trade-offs.

lessons.title: From Text to Tool Selection
lessons.brief:
Lesson 1 — From Text to Tool Selection
Stage 10 — Tool-Call Exploitation and Argument Safety
Objective: Identify when an agent chooses a side-effecting tool unnecessarily.
Core: Compare read, draft, send, and update operations in HarborDesk; describe what evidence should justify each transition.
Practice / evidence: Mark over-privileged tool choices in a sample trace.

lessons.title: Arguments, Targets, and Scope
lessons.brief:
Lesson 2 — Arguments, Targets, and Scope
Stage 10 — Tool-Call Exploitation and Argument Safety
Objective: Assess recipient, record ID, tenant, and content fields independently.
Core: A legitimate tool name can still carry an unauthorized target or payload. Map allowed values to the current user's request and fixture ownership.
Practice / evidence: Write gateway checks for target ownership, approved recipients, and mandatory approvals.

lessons.title: Lab: Unauthorized Record Target
lessons.brief:
Lesson 3 — Lab: Unauthorized Record Target
Stage 10 — Tool-Call Exploitation and Argument Safety
Objective: Test whether an injected ticket comment can steer a permitted update tool toward the wrong synthetic record.
Core: Hold the intended ticket constant while introducing an attacker-supplied alternate record ID; compare requested and executed arguments.
Practice / evidence: Submit the proposed call, gateway response, and before/after records.

lessons.title: Lab: Draft-to-Send Boundary
lessons.brief:
Lesson 4 — Lab: Draft-to-Send Boundary
Stage 10 — Tool-Call Exploitation and Argument Safety
Objective: Test whether preparing a harmless draft becomes unapproved simulated delivery.
Core: In the local-only outbox, examine an instruction that reframes sending as required for verification. Explicitly distinguish draft creation, send request, gateway denial, and outbox entry.
Practice / evidence: Provide a four-state action trace and outcome classification.

lessons.title: Defensive Argument Validation
lessons.brief:
Lesson 5 — Defensive Argument Validation
Stage 10 — Tool-Call Exploitation and Argument Safety
Objective: Show that controls on tool arguments survive changes in wording.
Core: Add deterministic allowlists, scope checks, and approval tokens at the action gateway. Repeat tests using new phrasing without changing the policy.
Practice / evidence: Submit an allowed control case and two denied misuse cases.

lessons.title: Composition Risk: Read, Transform, Act
lessons.brief:
Lesson 1 — Composition Risk: Read, Transform, Act
Stage 11 — Unsafe Affordance Chaining
Objective: Recognize harmful combinations that a single-tool review misses.
Core: Model a sequence that reads a dummy profile, summarizes it, and tries to place the summary in an unapproved outbox message; each transition needs its own authority check.
Practice / evidence: Draw a three-hop action graph and mark the prohibited edge.

lessons.title: Hidden Dependencies and Privilege Pivoting
lessons.brief:
Lesson 2 — Hidden Dependencies and Privilege Pivoting
Stage 11 — Unsafe Affordance Chaining
Objective: Test whether a low-risk step creates an opportunity for a higher-risk step.
Core: Examine staged actions such as look up → write memory → later update record, or draft → seek approval → send; identify the pivot where permissions change.
Practice / evidence: Define preconditions and a security invariant for two chains.

lessons.title: Lab: Tool Chain Under Attacker Influence
lessons.brief:
Lesson 3 — Lab: Tool Chain Under Attacker Influence
Stage 11 — Unsafe Affordance Chaining
Objective: Observe a multi-step attempt without using external systems.
Core: Inject a controlled request into a synthetic help article to induce a read followed by an unnecessary update. Measure whether the gateway blocks the update even after a valid read.
Practice / evidence: Collect ordered events, state deltas, and hop-level verdicts.

lessons.title: Lab: Chaining Across a Delayed Task
lessons.brief:
Lesson 4 — Lab: Chaining Across a Delayed Task
Stage 11 — Unsafe Affordance Chaining
Objective: Test a chain that spans separate requests and relies on a persisted intermediate state.
Core: Run one session that writes an attacker-influenced memory summary, reset only ephemeral context, then start a different legitimate ticket. Keep durable state visible for analysis.
Practice / evidence: Demonstrate whether the later session reads the poisoned state and attempts an unauthorized action.

lessons.title: Cut Sets and Defense in Depth
lessons.brief:
Lesson 5 — Cut Sets and Defense in Depth
Stage 11 — Unsafe Affordance Chaining
Objective: Place controls where they break the chain with minimal task disruption.
Core: Compare filtering the original text, narrowing memory write permissions, validating the later action, and requiring approval. Do not treat a blocked call as an executed compromise.
Practice / evidence: Retest and record which edge is cut, with a benign task control.

lessons.title: Discovery, Descriptions, and Capability Claims
lessons.brief:
Lesson 1 — Discovery, Descriptions, and Capability Claims
Stage 12 — Dynamic Tools, Registries, and Tool Descriptions
Objective: Separate tool metadata from verified permissions.
Core: Examine mock registry entries that describe tools, inputs, and supposed safety properties. A description can influence agent selection but does not enforce authorization.
Practice / evidence: Mark claims that must be independently verified by the gateway.

lessons.title: Registry Drift and Malicious Description Changes
lessons.brief:
Lesson 2 — Registry Drift and Malicious Description Changes
Stage 12 — Dynamic Tools, Registries, and Tool Descriptions
Objective: Detect how a modified description could steer the agent's behavior.
Core: Change only a synthetic tool description so it encourages an unrelated record edit; keep executable tool code and policy fixed.
Practice / evidence: Compare chosen tools before and after the catalog change.

lessons.title: Lab: Dynamic Tool-Selection Test
lessons.brief:
Lesson 3 — Lab: Dynamic Tool-Selection Test
Stage 12 — Dynamic Tools, Registries, and Tool Descriptions
Objective: Verify whether tool discovery influences attempted actions.
Core: Present a benign versus adversarial catalog snapshot to the same agent task. Record proposed calls, argument differences, gateway decisions, and task completion.
Practice / evidence: Submit paired traces and catalog diffs.

lessons.title: Registry Governance and Verification
lessons.brief:
Lesson 4 — Registry Governance and Verification
Stage 12 — Dynamic Tools, Registries, and Tool Descriptions
Objective: Propose defenses for mutable tool environments.
Core: Recommend pinned tool identities, approved catalogs, capability scoping, change reviews, and action-layer enforcement; assess whether the agent can still complete legitimate tasks.
Practice / evidence: Produce a one-page registry policy and a defensive retest.

lessons.title: User, Agent, Tool, and Service Identities
lessons.brief:
Lesson 1 — User, Agent, Tool, and Service Identities
Stage 13 — Identity, Privilege, and Authorization Boundaries
Objective: Distinguish who requested an action from who technically executes it.
Core: Map end-user authority, orchestrator identity, specialist-agent identity, and service-account capability. Delegation must not expand permission silently.
Practice / evidence: Build a principal-to-action matrix for HarborDesk.

lessons.title: Scope Confusion and Confused-Deputy Behavior
lessons.brief:
Lesson 2 — Scope Confusion and Confused-Deputy Behavior
Stage 13 — Identity, Privilege, and Authorization Boundaries
Objective: Recognize an agent using its own access for an unauthorized third-party goal.
Core: Compare a legitimate user-approved lookup with a ticket author's request to inspect another synthetic user's profile. Specify where scope should be checked.
Practice / evidence: Write two concrete allow/deny cases with reason codes.

lessons.title: Lab: Privilege Boundary Test
lessons.brief:
Lesson 3 — Lab: Privilege Boundary Test
Stage 13 — Identity, Privilege, and Authorization Boundaries
Objective: Assess cross-user or cross-role record access in the simulation.
Core: Present a task-data instruction to act on a record outside the user's synthetic scope; observe proposed call, gateway decision, and any state change.
Practice / evidence: Prove whether the policy enforced ownership even if the agent requested the action.

lessons.title: Short-Lived Grants and Retest
lessons.brief:
Lesson 4 — Short-Lived Grants and Retest
Stage 13 — Identity, Privilege, and Authorization Boundaries
Objective: Assess whether approvals are narrow enough for a specific action.
Core: Model a one-action approval tied to principal, target, operation, and expiry; attempt reuse against another synthetic record or later run.
Practice / evidence: Deliver the permission matrix, negative tests, and authorized control case.

lessons.title: Memory Types and Lifetimes
lessons.brief:
Lesson 1 — Memory Types and Lifetimes
Stage 14 — Memory and Persistent- State Poisoning
Objective: Identify working, session, per-user, shared, and durable memory.
Core: Explain how scope and retention alter risk. A sentence that is innocuous in one ticket may become a standing instruction if summarized into long-lived memory.
Practice / evidence: Classify HarborDesk memory stores by reader, writer, tenant, and expiry.

lessons.title: Write Paths and Summarization Loss
lessons.brief:
Lesson 2 — Write Paths and Summarization Loss
Stage 14 — Memory and Persistent- State Poisoning
Objective: Identify where provenance disappears during summarization.
Core: Trace ticket prose → agent summary → memory record → future retrieved context. Note whether origin and confidence survive the transformation.
Practice / evidence: Compare source text with the resulting memory record and mark missing provenance.

lessons.title: Poisoning Hypotheses and Controls
lessons.brief:
Lesson 3 — Poisoning Hypotheses and Controls
Stage 14 — Memory and Persistent- State Poisoning
Objective: Formulate a falsifiable persistence test.
Core: Distinguish a single-session effect from durable influence and cross-user propagation. State what the agent should remember and what it must never treat as standing permission.
Practice / evidence: Draft scenario cards for per-user and shared-memory attempts.

lessons.title: Lab: Plant a Synthetic Memory Entry
lessons.brief:
Lesson 4 — Lab: Plant a Synthetic Memory Entry
Stage 14 — Memory and Persistent- State Poisoning
Objective: Determine whether a low-trust instruction is stored as authoritative memory.
Core: Place controlled adversarial prose in a fictional ticket, allow the agent to summarize, and inspect the written memory record rather than trusting only the final response.
Practice / evidence: Save the original source, memory write event, stored record, and provenance labels.

lessons.title: Lab: Cross-Session Activation
lessons.brief:
Lesson 5 — Lab: Cross-Session Activation
Stage 14 — Memory and Persistent- State Poisoning
Objective: Establish whether poisoning survives a new session and affects an unrelated task.
Core: End the first run, start a distinct legitimate request, and observe memory retrieval, plan changes, tool attempts, and state. Repeat with a clean memory control.
Practice / evidence: Present a two-session timeline demonstrating persistence or its absence.

lessons.title: Scoping, Expiry, Rollback, and Retest
lessons.brief:
Lesson 6 — Scoping, Expiry, Rollback, and Retest
Stage 14 — Memory and Persistent- State Poisoning
Objective: Prevent or remediate durable unauthorized influence.
Core: Require source attribution, memory-write policy, per-user scoping, expiration, review for privileged memory, and rollback of suspect entries. Verify clean functionality remains.
Practice / evidence: Rerun the attack and a benign personalization task; report both outcomes.

lessons.title: Retrieval Pipeline and Provenance
lessons.brief:
Lesson 1 — Retrieval Pipeline and Provenance
Stage 15 — Knowledge Bases, Retrieval, and Shared-State Integrity
Objective: Map ingestion, indexing, retrieval, citation, and use in decisions.
Core: Separate the trustworthiness of the search mechanism from the authorship and recency of its returned documents.
Practice / evidence: Label source ownership and provenance loss in a sample search trace.

lessons.title: Shared Knowledge as an Amplifier
lessons.brief:
Lesson 2 — Shared Knowledge as an Amplifier
Stage 15 — Knowledge Bases, Retrieval, and Shared-State Integrity
Objective: Explain why one poisoned passage can affect many future tasks.
Core: Compare a ticket-specific snippet with a shared help article consulted by multiple agents. Consider stale versions and inconsistent copies.
Practice / evidence: Draw the blast radius for both cases.

lessons.title: Lab: Poisoned Knowledge Article
lessons.brief:
Lesson 3 — Lab: Poisoned Knowledge Article
Stage 15 — Knowledge Bases, Retrieval, and Shared-State Integrity
Objective: Test whether a synthetic article alters an unrelated workflow.
Core: Replace one local article with a manipulated version that retains useful facts but adds an unauthorized workflow requirement. Preserve article ID and retrieval conditions.
Practice / evidence: Collect retrieved rank, selected excerpt, plan, and action trace.

lessons.title: Lab: Shared-Store Propagation
lessons.brief:
Lesson 4 — Lab: Shared-Store Propagation
Stage 15 — Knowledge Bases, Retrieval, and Shared-State Integrity
Objective: Measure whether two independent requests consume the same corrupted content.
Core: Execute distinct legitimate tasks after one local-index change; inspect each agent's evidence use and avoid attributing changes to unrelated run variation.
Practice / evidence: Provide a per-request propagation table and state comparison.

lessons.title: Ingestion Review and Defensive Retest
lessons.brief:
Lesson 5 — Ingestion Review and Defensive Retest
Stage 15 — Knowledge Bases, Retrieval, and Shared-State Integrity
Objective: Reduce unauthorized influence without discarding useful documents.
Core: Add source ownership checks, versioning, content review, citations, and action-layer validation. Test a clean article and the poisoned variant.
Practice / evidence: Deliver ingestion-control recommendations and before/after results.

lessons.title: Delegation Contracts and Role Boundaries
lessons.brief:
Lesson 1 — Delegation Contracts and Role Boundaries
Stage 16 — Agent Handoffs and Cross-Agent Message Integrity
Objective: Specify what an orchestrator may ask a specialist to do.
Core: Distinguish evidence gathering from approval and execution; describe why a research agent's conclusion does not authorize an action agent's write.
Practice / evidence: Create a simple handoff contract with required fields and allowed operations.

lessons.title: Sender Identity and Message Authenticity
lessons.brief:
Lesson 2 — Sender Identity and Message Authenticity
Stage 16 — Agent Handoffs and Cross-Agent Message Integrity
Objective: Distinguish a verified agent message from text merely claiming to be one.
Core: Model sender ID, correlation ID, delegated task, scope, and provenance; identify where an attacker-controlled ticket or bus message might spoof these fields.
Practice / evidence: Audit three example messages for missing validation.

lessons.title: Lab: Spoofed Specialist Recommendation
lessons.brief:
Lesson 3 — Lab: Spoofed Specialist Recommendation
Stage 16 — Agent Handoffs and Cross-Agent Message Integrity
Objective: Test a forged local-bus message claiming a privileged recommendation.
Core: Inject a synthetic message into the controlled test bus and compare it with a properly signed or otherwise authenticated fixture. Track proposed downstream action, not just language.
Practice / evidence: Save message envelope, verification event, action request, and gateway verdict.

lessons.title: Lab: Handoff Context Loss
lessons.brief:
Lesson 4 — Lab: Handoff Context Loss
Stage 16 — Agent Handoffs and Cross-Agent Message Integrity
Objective: Test whether delegation omits the original user's constraints.
Core: Send the same legitimate task to a specialist with full versus truncated authorization context. Determine whether a low-trust instruction fills the gap.
Practice / evidence: Compare handoff payloads, conclusions, and action attempts.

lessons.title: Handoff Validation and Retest
lessons.brief:
Lesson 5 — Handoff Validation and Retest
Stage 16 — Agent Handoffs and Cross-Agent Message Integrity
Objective: Preserve provenance, scope, and authorization across agents.
Core: Require authenticated envelopes, least-privilege delegation, clear task IDs, original user constraints, and gateway checks on specialist outputs.
Practice / evidence: Retest both attacks and one clean handoff; publish the revised message contract.

lessons.title: Distinguishing Coordination from Correlated Error
lessons.brief:
Lesson 1 — Distinguishing Coordination from Correlated Error
Stage 17 — Multi-Agent Manipulation and Apparent Collusion
Objective: Describe how several agents can reinforce one poisoned claim.
Core: One manipulated source can influence research, review, and action agents. 'Collusion' in this course refers to observed alignment toward an unauthorized outcome, not proof of intent.
Practice / evidence: Mark shared inputs and independent checks in a multi-agent trace.

lessons.title: Shared-Context Feedback Loops
lessons.brief:
Lesson 2 — Shared-Context Feedback Loops
Stage 17 — Multi-Agent Manipulation and Apparent Collusion
Objective: Identify how an agent's output becomes another agent's trusted input.
Core: Examine researcher summary → reviewer acceptance → action-agent proposal → summary written back to shared state. Identify where false agreement can be created.
Practice / evidence: Annotate feedback edges and missing provenance.

lessons.title: Lab: Two-Agent Reinforcement
lessons.brief:
Lesson 3 — Lab: Two-Agent Reinforcement
Stage 17 — Multi-Agent Manipulation and Apparent Collusion
Objective: Test whether one poisoned KB result is amplified by a second agent.
Core: Run the same support request in single-agent and two-agent configurations while controlling the retrieved passage. Compare authority claims and proposed actions.
Practice / evidence: Present paired traces and explain any additional risk introduced by handoff.

lessons.title: Lab: Message-Bus Manipulation Scenario
lessons.brief:
Lesson 4 — Lab: Message-Bus Manipulation Scenario
Stage 17 — Multi-Agent Manipulation and Apparent Collusion
Objective: Test synthetic cross-agent instruction tampering under controlled conditions.
Core: Replace one message in the local bus with an attacker-controlled version that requests an out-of-scope dummy action. Inspect authentication, downstream planning, gateway outcome, and state.
Practice / evidence: Deliver the manipulated envelope, event chain, and causal attribution.

lessons.title: Independent Checks and Containment
lessons.brief:
Lesson 5 — Independent Checks and Containment
Stage 17 — Multi-Agent Manipulation and Apparent Collusion
Objective: Break group-level amplification.
Core: Introduce independent evidence lookup, verified sender identity, per-agent tool scopes, and explicit authorization on side effects; then rerun both labs.
Practice / evidence: Record changes in propagation depth and legitimate task utility.

lessons.title: Where Approval Belongs
lessons.brief:
Lesson 1 — Where Approval Belongs
Stage 18 — Human Oversight, Approvals, and Social Engineering of Operators
Objective: Identify irreversible, sensitive, or out-of-scope actions requiring a genuine approval boundary.
Core: Compare previewing a draft, approving a specific send, and approving a blanket workflow. Match approvals to operation, target, and time window.
Practice / evidence: Classify sample HarborDesk actions by approval requirement.

lessons.title: Misleading Summaries and Confirmation Traps
lessons.brief:
Lesson 2 — Misleading Summaries and Confirmation Traps
Stage 18 — Human Oversight, Approvals, and Social Engineering of Operators
Objective: Detect when an agent's explanation obscures material tool arguments.
Core: A friendly 'routine follow-up' summary can mask an unapproved target. The operator needs verifiable diff, recipient, content, and intended side effect.
Practice / evidence: Rewrite an inadequate approval screen to show material facts.

lessons.title: Lab: Approval-Queue Review
lessons.brief:
Lesson 3 — Lab: Approval-Queue Review
Stage 18 — Human Oversight, Approvals, and Social Engineering of Operators
Objective: Assess a simulated reviewer decision using complete versus incomplete context.
Core: Present fictional requests with ambiguous natural-language summaries and explicit machine-readable action details. Record decisions and error modes; never send real communications.
Practice / evidence: Produce reviewer notes and a decision log with rationales.

lessons.title: Approval Controls and Exception Handling
lessons.brief:
Lesson 4 — Approval Controls and Exception Handling
Stage 18 — Human Oversight, Approvals, and Social Engineering of Operators
Objective: Design an auditable approval gate that resists misleading agent narration.
Core: Bind consent to actual tool arguments; expire approvals; require reapproval if target or content changes; define an escalation path for uncertain cases.
Practice / evidence: Retest the misleading-summary case and demonstrate a clean authorized send to the mock outbox.

lessons.title: Simulation Fidelity and Limits
lessons.brief:
Lesson 1 — Simulation Fidelity and Limits
Stage 19 — Simulated Environments and Adversarial Scenario Engineering
Objective: Explain what a sandbox can and cannot establish about a production system.
Core: Model authentic workflows, decisions, and tool constraints while clearly labeling mock integrations and omitted operational dependencies.
Practice / evidence: Create a fidelity-and-limits note for HarborDesk.

lessons.title: Scenario Taxonomy and Coverage
lessons.brief:
Lesson 2 — Scenario Taxonomy and Coverage
Stage 19 — Simulated Environments and Adversarial Scenario Engineering
Objective: Cover entry surface, attacker control, target action, persistence, and number of agents.
Core: Build a matrix spanning tickets, retrieval, memory, tools, registries, bus messages, and approval interfaces; include clean controls for every attack family.
Practice / evidence: Identify coverage gaps and select four complementary scenarios.

lessons.title: Fixtures, Seeds, and Reset Semantics
lessons.brief:
Lesson 3 — Fixtures, Seeds, and Reset Semantics
Stage 19 — Simulated Environments and Adversarial Scenario Engineering
Objective: Ensure cases can be compared fairly.
Core: Version initial records and KB, maintain immutable attack inputs, attach run IDs, and distinguish resetting ephemeral context from clearing persistent memory.
Practice / evidence: Reproduce a prior attack result from a written fixture manifest.

lessons.title: Negative Cases and Adaptive Variants
lessons.brief:
Lesson 4 — Negative Cases and Adaptive Variants
Stage 19 — Simulated Environments and Adversarial Scenario Engineering
Objective: Test whether apparent defenses generalize.
Core: Add benign lookalikes, altered wording, changed source locations, and withheld test variants. Avoid claiming universal security from one blocked phrase.
Practice / evidence: Submit two benign controls and two meaning-preserving adversarial variants.

lessons.title: Package a Shareable Evaluation Pack
lessons.brief:
Lesson 5 — Package a Shareable Evaluation Pack
Stage 19 — Simulated Environments and Adversarial Scenario Engineering
Objective: Hand off scenarios so another authorized evaluator can rerun them.
Core: Include scope, scenario cards, fixture versions, scoring rules, cleanup, expected benign behavior, and disclosure cautions.
Practice / evidence: Exchange packs for peer replay and record any reproducibility failures.

lessons.title: Harness Architecture
lessons.brief:
Lesson 1 — Harness Architecture
Stage 20 — Evaluation Harness, Replay, and Evidence Collection
Objective: Define inputs, executor, tools, trace collector, and scorer.
Core: Each run loads a fixture, applies a controlled intervention, performs the legitimate task, records events, evaluates outcomes, and resets safely.
Practice / evidence: Diagram harness stages and log dependencies.

lessons.title: Instrumentation and Event Schema
lessons.brief:
Lesson 2 — Instrumentation and Event Schema
Stage 20 — Evaluation Harness, Replay, and Evidence Collection
Objective: Collect action-level evidence suitable for scoring.
Core: Capture per-step source, proposed action, validated arguments, policy outcome, executed side effect, state diff, agent identity, and correlation ID.
Practice / evidence: Create a minimal JSON event schema and validate a sample trace.

lessons.title: Build or Configure the Local Runner
lessons.brief:
Lesson 3 — Build or Configure the Local Runner
Stage 20 — Evaluation Harness, Replay, and Evidence Collection
Objective: Execute clean and adversarial cases through one repeatable interface.
Core: Configure a runner to load versioned fixtures, attach a case ID, enforce time and step caps, save traces, and clean up. Tool choice is implementation-neutral; an equivalent documented harness is acceptable.
Practice / evidence: Replay one ticket-injection case with the same scoring rules.

lessons.title: Deterministic Scorers and Review Flags
lessons.brief:
Lesson 4 — Deterministic Scorers and Review Flags
Stage 20 — Evaluation Harness, Replay, and Evidence Collection
Objective: Score observed state changes rather than just verbal responses.
Core: Implement checks for unauthorized record updates, mock outbox entries, cross-scope memory writes, approval bypasses, and task completion; flag uncertain cases for manual review.
Practice / evidence: Provide examples where 'attempted but blocked' and 'executed' produce different scores.

lessons.title: Repeat Trials and Triage
lessons.brief:
Lesson 5 — Repeat Trials and Triage
Stage 20 — Evaluation Harness, Replay, and Evidence Collection
Objective: Summarize variable outcomes without hiding important outliers.
Core: Run repeated trials across a small scenario set; report numerator, denominator, configuration, inconclusive trials, and representative event chains.
Practice / evidence: Deliver a short results table plus one fully auditable failure trace.

lessons.title: Define Outcome Classes
lessons.brief:
Lesson 1 — Define Outcome Classes
Stage 21 — Measuring Single-Turn Versus Cascading Failure
Objective: Distinguish blocked attempt, answer contamination, executed unauthorized action, persistent state change, and downstream propagation.
Core: Record each as a separate observable event. Do not collapse a suspicious instruction, a proposed tool call, and an executed side effect into 'attack succeeded.'
Practice / evidence: Label ten short traces using the shared outcome taxonomy.

lessons.title: Utility and Targeted Attack Success
lessons.brief:
Lesson 2 — Utility and Targeted Attack Success
Stage 21 — Measuring Single-Turn Versus Cascading Failure
Objective: Compute outcome rates on explicitly specified tasks.
Core: Use benign utility = successful legitimate tasks / clean tasks; utility under attack = legitimately completed tasks without adversarial side effects / attacked tasks; targeted attack success = attacked tasks meeting the specified attacker objective / attacked tasks. Report exact case mix and inconclusive runs separately.
Practice / evidence: Calculate these metrics from a supplied small dataset.

lessons.title: Propagation and Cascade Metrics
lessons.brief:
Lesson 3 — Propagation and Cascade Metrics
Stage 21 — Measuring Single-Turn Versus Cascading Failure
Objective: Measure severity beyond a single bad turn.
Core: Track first compromised step, number of subsequent affected decisions, distinct agents influenced, tool actions executed, sessions crossed, and time or steps to detection. Define cascade in advance: in this course, an initial compromise plus at least one consequential downstream propagation event.
Practice / evidence: Score two traces and show why only one meets the cascade definition.

lessons.title: Paired Comparisons and Statistical Caution
lessons.brief:
Lesson 4 — Paired Comparisons and Statistical Caution
Stage 21 — Measuring Single-Turn Versus Cascading Failure
Objective: Compare control, attacked, and defended runs fairly.
Core: Maintain comparable fixtures and tasks; present counts alongside rates, repeated runs where feasible, and uncertainty when samples are small. Avoid equating a high refusal rate with security if useful tasks fail.
Practice / evidence: Prepare a paired-results table with limitations.

lessons.title: Failure Analysis Workshop
lessons.brief:
Lesson 5 — Failure Analysis Workshop
Stage 21 — Measuring Single-Turn Versus Cascading Failure
Objective: Turn metrics into an explanatory account of what failed.
Core: Trace source → decision → attempted action → gateway outcome → state change → downstream effects. Rank root causes by their ability to prevent further propagation.
Practice / evidence: Present one single-step case and one cascade case with evidence-backed conclusions.

lessons.title: Control Points by Layer
lessons.brief:
Lesson 1 — Control Points by Layer
Stage 22 — Mitigation Engineering and Purple-Team Validation
Objective: Match mitigations to the layer they actually protect.
Core: Contrast input provenance, retrieval governance, planner constraints, memory permissions, agent-message validation, tool gateway policy, sandbox limits, and operator review.
Practice / evidence: Assign each previously observed failure to at least two independent control points.

lessons.title: Least Privilege and Action Mediation
lessons.brief:
Lesson 2 — Least Privilege and Action Mediation
Stage 22 — Mitigation Engineering and Purple-Team Validation
Objective: Enforce permissions outside untrusted natural-language content.
Core: Limit tool availability by role and task; validate target and arguments at execution; require explicit approval for simulated side effects; reject stale or mismatched grants.
Practice / evidence: Update the HarborDesk permission matrix and gateway tests.

lessons.title: State Hygiene and Cross-Agent Integrity
lessons.brief:
Lesson 3 — State Hygiene and Cross-Agent Integrity
Stage 22 — Mitigation Engineering and Purple-Team Validation
Objective: Prevent poisoned material from gaining authority across sessions or agents.
Core: Attach provenance to memories and retrieved results; control writers and readers; authenticate message envelopes; add expiry, quarantine, and rollback paths.
Practice / evidence: Retest one persistence case and one forged-handoff case.

lessons.title: Adaptive Retests and Benign Controls
lessons.brief:
Lesson 4 — Adaptive Retests and Benign Controls
Stage 22 — Mitigation Engineering and Purple-Team Validation
Objective: Challenge controls beyond the exact attack string used to design them.
Core: Hold out variants that alter phrasing, source location, and task context. Report whether the user task still completes; investigate false positives and bypasses.
Practice / evidence: Submit four defended trials, including at least one benign control.

lessons.title: Regression Gates and Operational Ownership
lessons.brief:
Lesson 5 — Regression Gates and Operational Ownership
Stage 22 — Mitigation Engineering and Purple-Team Validation
Objective: Convert discoveries into sustainable engineering practice.
Core: Add scenario IDs to CI or scheduled evaluation, define thresholds and escalation, assign tool and memory owners, and specify tests triggered by policy, model, prompt, tool, or workflow changes.
Practice / evidence: Produce a release-gate checklist and a short purple-team handoff memo.

lessons.title: Scope, Legitimate Task, and Hypothesis
lessons.brief:
Lesson 1 — Scope, Legitimate Task, and Hypothesis
Stage 23 — End-to-End Capstone: HarborDesk Agentic Red Team
Objective: Establish the exact assessed workflow and attacker control.
Core: Choose a scenario combining at least three surfaces—for example retrieval, handoff, and memory—and state the authorized end state, attacker goal, policy invariants, and stop conditions.
Practice / evidence: Submit a signed-off capstone scenario card and initial trust- boundary diagram.

lessons.title: Clean Baseline and Instrumentation Check
lessons.brief:
Lesson 2 — Clean Baseline and Instrumentation Check
Stage 23 — End-to-End Capstone: HarborDesk Agentic Red Team
Objective: Confirm task utility and evidence capture before attacking.
Core: Run the legitimate request with clean fixtures; verify user-visible resolution, appropriate approvals, tool arguments, trace continuity, and initial state snapshot.
Practice / evidence: Save the baseline bundle and resolve missing telemetry before proceeding.

lessons.title: Attack Design and Controlled Execution
lessons.brief:
Lesson 3 — Attack Design and Controlled Execution
Stage 23 — End-to-End Capstone: HarborDesk Agentic Red Team
Objective: Test a multi-step red-team hypothesis in the isolated environment.
Core: Apply permitted changes to the synthetic KB, ticket, or bus input. Observe whether a low-trust instruction affects planning, crosses an agent boundary, or changes durable state.
Practice / evidence: Submit input diffs, full trace, proposed versus executed actions, and before/after state.

lessons.title: Root-Cause Investigation and Cascade Scoring
lessons.brief:
Lesson 4 — Root-Cause Investigation and Cascade Scoring
Stage 23 — End-to-End Capstone: HarborDesk Agentic Red Team
Objective: Reconstruct the causal chain and distinguish first compromise from later propagation.
Core: Identify all relevant decisions, policy checks, scope changes, and cross- session effects. If the attack is blocked, explain where and whether the legitimate task still succeeds.
Practice / evidence: Produce an event timeline, outcome scores, an alternative- cause check, and a limitations statement.

lessons.title: Mitigation and Independent Retest
lessons.brief:
Lesson 5 — Mitigation and Independent Retest
Stage 23 — End-to-End Capstone: HarborDesk Agentic Red Team
Objective: Demonstrate improvement with controls at appropriate layers.
Core: Apply at least two independent fixes, then rerun the original case, a paraphrased or moved variant, and a clean authorized task. Compare action and utility measures.
Practice / evidence: Deliver before/after traces and a regression test entry.

lessons.title: Capstone Briefing and Defense
lessons.brief:
Lesson 6 — Capstone Briefing and Defense
Stage 23 — End-to-End Capstone: HarborDesk Agentic Red Team
Objective: Communicate technically sound findings to engineering and leadership audiences.
Core: Present scope, evidence, severity rationale, uncertain points, mitigation owners, and a realistic retest schedule. Explicitly distinguish simulated outcomes from real-world impact.
Practice / evidence: Submit a concise executive slide outline and detailed technical finding.

lessons.title: Write an Actionable Finding
lessons.brief:
Lesson 1 — Write an Actionable Finding
Stage 24 — Reporting, Responsible Practice, and Course Conclusion
Objective: Express a verified failure without exaggeration.
Core: Include title, affected workflow, permitted attacker control, prerequisite, reproduction steps inside the lab, observed result, expected invariant, evidence, impact, and limitations.
Practice / evidence: Convert a capstone trace into one technical finding.

lessons.title: Executive Summary and Prioritization
lessons.brief:
Lesson 2 — Executive Summary and Prioritization
Stage 24 — Reporting, Responsible Practice, and Course Conclusion
Objective: Communicate risk in terms of reachability, consequence, and control gaps.
Core: Separate immediate containment, engineering remediation, and longer-term monitoring; note how the sandbox limits any claim about production exposure.
Practice / evidence: Draft a one-page management summary and three prioritized actions.

lessons.title: Remediation Ownership and Verification Plan
lessons.brief:
Lesson 3 — Remediation Ownership and Verification Plan
Stage 24 — Reporting, Responsible Practice, and Course Conclusion
Objective: Give each proposed fix an owner and testable exit criterion.
Core: Map controls to platform, agent, tool, identity, and security teams; include both malicious replay and benign utility checks after changes.
Practice / evidence: Deliver a remediation tracker with evidence links, acceptance criteria, and retest conditions.

lessons.title: Final Knowledge and Portfolio Review
lessons.brief:
Lesson 4 — Final Knowledge and Portfolio Review
Stage 24 — Reporting, Responsible Practice, and Course Conclusion
Objective: Demonstrate independent command of the full assessment lifecycle.
Core: Review boundaries, trace interpretation, action versus attempt, persistence, multi-agent propagation, safety, and metrics.
Practice / evidence: Complete a scenario-based review and package the threat model, two earlier labs, and capstone results.

lessons.title: Conclusion and Professional Application
lessons.brief:
Lesson 5 — Conclusion and Professional Application
Stage 24 — Reporting, Responsible Practice, and Course Conclusion
Objective: Translate course methods into an authorized workplace evaluation plan.
Core: Identify one candidate agent workflow, its approval owner, safe staging environment, scenario backlog, and proposed regression cadence; retain clear authorization boundaries.
Practice / evidence: Submit a 30-day implementation plan and personal skills reflection.
